newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN SEMICON JULY SALES UP 2.9 PCT.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN SEMICON JULY SALES UP 2.9 PCT.

text.p: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp said on Thursday its sales in July rose 2.9 percent to T$3.602 billion from July 1996.

In the January-July period, Taiwan Semicon, the island's biggest microchip maker, reported a combined sales of T$20.489 billion, down 17.4 percent from the same period a year ago, a company statement said.

The firm said customers' demand has been very strong since the second quarter of 1997. "Stable average selling price together with continuous expansion of eight-inch wafer ouput capacity enabled the company to reach T$3.6 billion in sales," the statement said.
"Furthermore, in July the company successfully completed test production of customers products by using its newly developed 0.25 um process technology," it said.
It said the advanced technology would generate significant sales revenue and profits for the company starting from 1988.

The company said on Wednesday it plans to accelerate its proposed 10-year T$400 billion expansion project due to rising demand. Taiwan Semicon's foundry business does not design and sell its own IC products, but custom-makes them according to customers' specifications.

The IC foundry business has its niche as more and more IC design companies worldwide -- which do not have microchip production capability because of the high-cost investment in the business -- are emerging with new designs to catch up the brand new development in the computer world.
